content.title: About
content.content: Okra (Abelmoschus esculentus) is an edible pod of a tropical and subtropical plant. Fresh pods are typically green, 10–20 cm long, with tender flesh and tiny edible seeds. They can be eaten raw, but are most often cooked—boiled, stewed, fried, or sautéed with added fat to enhance flavor and nutrient absorption.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Okra is known by many names: lady’s finger, gumbo, and “vegetable silk”.
It has been cultivated in Africa and Southeast Asia for over 4,000 years.
The mucilaginous compounds in okra give soups and stews a thick, glossy texture.
In the United States, okra is a staple of Southern cuisine, especially in gumbo.
Pods come in a range of colors, from bright green to yellow and even purple.

items.title: High in dietary fiber
items.content: Fiber supports healthy digestion and promotes a feeling of fullness.

items.title: Source of vitamin C
items.content: Vitamin C boosts immunity and aids collagen synthesis.

items.title: Contains vitamin K
items.content: Vitamin K is essential for blood clotting and bone health.

items.title: Rich in antioxidants
items.content: Flavonoids and carotenoids protect cells from oxidative stress.

items.title: May help regulate blood sugar
items.content: The mucilage slows carbohydrate absorption, helping to stabilize glucose levels.

items.title: Allergic reactions
items.content: Some individuals may experience skin rashes or swelling after consuming okra.

items.title: Oxalate content
items.content: Okra contains oxalates, which can contribute to kidney stone formation in susceptible people.

items.title: Digestive issues when raw
items.content: Raw okra’s high mucilage can cause stomach discomfort; cooking reduces this effect.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Okra can be steamed, boiled, added to soups, stews, and curries, or sautéed with a little oil, which improves flavor and aids absorption of fat‑soluble vitamins. Raw pods are suitable for salads when sliced thinly and marinated to reduce slime.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Store fresh okra in the refrigerator in a plastic bag or container; it stays crisp for up to 5 days. For longer storage, blanch the pods for 2–3 minutes and freeze them.
